Subject: Arbor Health – private deploy workflow exception and scope asks

Team —

Following the discovery call with Arbor Health yesterday, they want to move forward with a private (VPC) deployment but one item came up that will require an exception to our standard pilot lane: they need all inference to remain in-region and processed on-prem for a subset of PHI-adjacent workloads.

Attached: Arbor_SOW_draft_v1.pdf, network-diagram.png.

High-level asks from Sales/Customer:
- Pilot timeline: 8–12 weeks preferred.
- Minimal SLA for pilot (48/7 support) and a clear escalation path.
- Evidence: SOC2 + audit log export and KMS integration for customer keys.

What I need from eng/security/product:
1) A quick feasibility note on whether this can be accommodated under our Private product (VPC + on-prem bundle) without multi-month infra changes.
2) A list of exception gates we should require before starting (security artifacts, staffing, infra sizing).
3) Rough ops/resource estimate so we can firm the SOW and propose a timeline to Arbor.

Can folks reply into this thread by Monday EOD? I’ll coordinate the next call with Rajiv and their security lead.

—Monica

Thanks Monica — looping in Product and Eng to capture constraints. A few quick clarifying Qs before we dive into sizing:

- Does Arbor require a hard air-gap (no internet egress) or just in-region with strict egress controls? (Rajiv, can you confirm?)
- Are they expecting us to manage hardware as part of the pilot or will they provide a partner-managed rack?

1) Run a 12-week pilot under the "exception" lane with a clearly documented rollback (fall back to hosted variants) and only for named workloads.
2) Engineering provides an ops/minimum-resource checklist and a proposed runbook.
3) Security signs off on gating artifacts (KMS, logging, penetration test scope).

Markus — can you do an architecture sketch + minimum GPU/ops asks? Kimberly — can you list the security gating artifacts we need to get to green? Grace — I want Product to weigh in on which features must be gated (model pinning, quantization profiles, logging granularity).

Quick architecture + ops notes (first pass):

Summary: feasible as a Private/VPC + on-prem extension but requires a small set of nontrivial items: dedicated GPU nodes (for latency/SLO), ops oncall commitment, network ACLs and cross-connect, and an ingress filtering + egress policy.

Minimum technical checklist (pilot):
- GPU footprint: 4x80GB-class GPUs (A100/4xH100 equivalence) for baseline 50 RPS gen + headroom. If Arbor can accept smaller quantized models, we can reduce to 2x80GB with throughput degradation.
- Storage: 10TB NVMe for model cache + KV cache persistence.
- Networking: cross-connect (VLAN) to their environment; BGP optional for redundancy. Must support private peering and customer-managed firewall rules (we will provide IP ranges).
- Key management: customer KMS (bring-your-own-key) integration — recommend vault + HSM-backed KMS.
- Observability: per-request trace IDs, token-level cost breakdown (scrubbed), and near-real-time audit log export (syslog/Splunk).
- Fallback path: define model variant (lower cost/latency) to route to Hosted in region only if on-prem capacity is exhausted — but this will require contractual agreement with Arbor for data flows.

Ops/people asks:
- 1x SRE lead (8–12 weeks) + 0.5 FTE platform engineer for pilot setup and tuning.
- Oncall: we need a 2-week rotation commitment from Redwood support team and a named escalation matrix.

Open questions that affect timeline/price:
- Are we allowed to run continuous batching/auto-scaling in-customer environment? If not, throughput is fixed and costs increase.
- Will Arbor accept outside-of-hours deployments or do we need to coordinate maintenance windows?

I started a very small resource workbook (ops-resource-estimate.xlsx) — will update with cost ranges once we have clarity on the quantization/throughput requirement.

—Markus
Staff Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Security checklist (pilot gating items):

Must-haves before pilot kickoff:
- KMS: customer-managed keys with HSM-backed KMS; we need key rotation policy and ACL document.
- Audit logs: retention policy (minimum 12 months) and export path to customer SIEM (we provide syslog endpoint).
- Network: allowlist + deny-by-default firewall rules; no public IPs on inference nodes.
- Vulnerability baseline: run an internal vulnerability scan and provide PV reports; customer may request penetration test (we will support).
- Data residency: confirm datasets that will be processed on-prem; any PHI flagged data must be isolated and not leave the cluster.

Recommended controls to include in SOW:
- Continuous monitoring with alerting thresholds and a named security contact on both sides.
- A brief SOC2 addendum describing the exception lane controls (we can provide a template).

Open items for Arbor:
- Will their security team accept our standard SOC2 evidence or do they need additional artifacts (e.g., network diagrams with subnet ranges, specific encryption cipher lists)?
- Do they require mutual TLS for internal service-to-service traffic?

If they confirm the above quickly, Security can sign off in 4–5 business days.

—Kimberly
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple clarifications from our side: 
- We need in-region processing only; we are not asking for a fully air-gapped network but strict egress controls such that nothing marked PHI leaves our environment.
- We will provide a partner-managed rack with empty slots and basic power; we expect Redwood to handle OS, runtime, and model installs.
- Timeline: 10–12 weeks is preferred (pilot must be complete before our next compliance audit window).

Priya (copied) is our security lead — she will review your checklist and send any additional artifacts. We would like a short call Friday to align on the network firewall rules and KMS integration.

—Rajiv
Head of Cloud Engineering, Arbor Health

Internal summary + decision: proceed with exception-lane pilot

Based on the customer clarifications and internal feasibility notes, we will proceed with a 12-week pilot under an "exception" lane with the following decision points and owners:

1) Security gating (owner: Kimberly Park) — deliver KMS integration checklist, audit log endpoints, and SOC2 addendum by 2026-10-20.
2) Architecture & ops (owner: Markus Klein) — confirm final sizing and provide runbook + resource workbook by 2026-10-22.
3) Product scope (owner: Grace O'Connor) — identify the exact feature subset to enable (model pinning, logging granularity) and sign off by 2026-10-21.
4) Sales/SOW (owner: Monica Patel) — finalize pilot SOW and DocuSign link (DOCUSIGN://arbor-sow-8342) and get Arbor signature no later than 2026-10-29.
5) Kickoff call with Arbor security (owner: Monica/Rishi) — schedule for Fri 2026-10-16; Monica please lock time.

Notes: Ops estimate workbook, network diagram, and draft SOW are attached. We will treat any deviation from the gating items as a scope change and pause deployments until remediation.

Next steps: Monica to schedule kickoff; Markus/Kimberly/Grace to review the attachments and drop comments in the Drive doc (https://drive.redwood.local/ArborHealth/PrivateDeployRoadmap).

Rishi
